item.title: Visión audaz
item.dc:creator: xynova
item.description: El líder decreta que la gravedad es opcional para los ciudadanos leales. El ministerio no cuestiona su contacto con la realidad: prefiere organizar un taller sobre la tipografía de las notas al pie y se olvida de llamar al psiquiatra.
item.sync:pageSocial:
"Bold Vision"
❓ The leader declares gravity optional for loyal citizens. The ministry does not question his contact with reality; it schedules a workshop on footnote typography and forgets to call the psychiatrist.
AND: At the podium he announces a law that physics politely refuses to obey. The ants reach for a thesaurus and call the moment ambition. Frog clerks open an implementation binder and argue about Arial versus the new national serif. Compliance wants a timeline; procurement wants a vendor; communications wants a tagline. Nobody asks whether the words describe the world.
🟣 W27: Reptilocracy 🦎🏛️
This is part of an experiment: we are keeping count of how many scenes it takes before we agree that leaders with real power should prove they are psychologically fit to hold it.
By turning our instincts and hive habits into animals, the project asks why we still let untested nervous systems run entire societies.
One concrete step: sign the Change.org petition for stronger checks and psychological fitness standards for Australia's top leaders.

item.title: La mona, aunque se vista de seda, mona se queda.
item.dc:creator: xynova
item.description: Cada año un negocio nuevo, y nadie ha recuperado un centavo.
item.sync:pageSocial:
"La mona, aunque se vista de seda, mona se queda."
❓ It describes people who want to pretend they are something they are not. They put on the silk, try and try and try, and they are still the same old monkey. A coworker shows up with a new car, then tailored suits, then a new title, and still hands the real work to the interns. When a deadline slips, the intern stays late and takes the client's complaint while the coworker collects the credit.
AND: It is the tired shrug of someone who has watched the same person try again and again and come out unchanged. You say it about the cousin who announces a new venture every year and has never paid anyone back. Nobody argues, because everyone has already seen the last three versions.
🔤 IN ENGLISH: • All hat and no cattle • Lipstick on a pig • You can't make a silk purse out of a sow's ear

item.title: La etiqueta no es un mapa, es un techo
item.dc:creator: xynova
item.description: Una clínica puede cerrar el expediente de un niño tras un solo diagnóstico y no revisar movimiento, lenguaje ni traumatismos. El colegio suele planificar el año con una sola etiqueta, y el resto de lo que le cuesta al niño no entra en la derivación. Los maestros pueden pasar el curso entero con una casilla que cubre solo una parte de lo que el niño necesita.
item.sync:pageSocial:
A single label is a ceiling rather than a map
A clinician says one word at the school gate, and the relief in the room makes everyone stop asking what else the child struggles with. The teacher plans the term around attention while movement, speech, and sleep never make it onto the form.
✜ Clinics often match symptoms to one checklist and treat that word as the whole profile. UK NICE expects autism assessments to cover coexisting conditions and motor problems, yet many files still close after the first label that fits.
✜ Local agencies run support in sequence. Funding and referrals attach to the paper that arrived, so a pupil with a language gap and an attention label may get help for focus alone while the next door stays shut for months.
✜ UK research puts developmental language disorder around one child in thirteen, and mainstream schools often steer more support toward autism than toward language needs at the same severity.
✜ Clinicians who skip head injury history often match focus problems to ADHD while a past injury stays off the chart. NICE treats acquired brain injury as part of that same assessment picture.
✜ The child waiting outside the head teacher's office pays for that one-label model every day. Parents can ask which movement screen and head injury history ran before the label landed. They can also ask the school for one everyday fix, a pencil grip or a seat near the door, while the second check waits.
The word sets the ceiling for what staff will measure. The child still walks in with every gap the first screen skipped.

item.title: No cruces la mirada
item.dc:creator: xynova
item.description: Las provincias pueden quedar reducidas a cenizas, pero la burocracia solo piensa en la vuelta a casa. La institución mantiene la continuidad: trata un brote psicótico como una reunión que no acaba nunca.
item.sync:pageSocial:
🦎🏛️ No cruces la mirada con quien sostiene el sello de emergencia.
El expediente oficial habla de "retórica apasionada" en la sesión de la tarde. Nadie anota la espuma por la boca, porque el comité de aptitud psicológica jamás ha entrado en el calendario.
Así que los funcionarios aprenden otra habilidad: escurrirse hacia la puerta sin cruzar la mirada con quien puede sellar la crisis. En esos pasillos, visionario y lunático son sobre todo cuestión de horario de oficina.
La institución no exige una mente estable en el podio. Solo exige que el colapso termine antes de la hora de salida.
#Reptilocracy #NarrativeControl #AccountabilityGap #Leadership #PsychFitness

item.title: 🌊 Construimos arcas para los negacionistas más ruidosos
item.dc:creator: xynova
item.description: Nuestra fe en el excepcionalismo humano esconde los límites biológicos que empujan nuestros fracasos. Construimos arcas para los negacionistas más ruidosos y tratamos la inundación como problema de otros.
item.sync:pageSocial:
🌊 We build arks for the loudest deniers
We assume our intelligence makes us immune to natural limits. In reality, we are just apes with high-voltage tools, pretending the water isn't rising.
✜ In the older flood story, Atrahasis, the gods wiped out humanity because our noise ruined their sleep. That myth casts us as a loud biological population that exhausts its own environment, and that diagnosis still holds up today.
✜ Biologist Ajit Varki names the mental shield we rely on: the Mind Over Reality Transition (MORT). Self-awareness required a biological reflex to deny unbearable truths so we could keep functioning, and modern cities now use that same reflex to ignore rising seas and keep business running.
✜ Our biological hardware also clashes with our tools. A manager steering a global supply chain feels the same cortisol spike from a critical email that an ancestor felt when spotting a predator in the brush, which leaves planetary systems running on stone-age anxieties.
✜ We repeat that selection error in the modern lifeboats we build, from private bunkers to Mars plans and walled estates. Because entry goes to wealth and political influence, we are building ships for the people best at pretending the water is still calm.
Are we selecting for sanity or for noise? A vessel steered by skilled deniers is just the old world, floating.
#Denial #RealityCheck #Leadership #StatusIsNotSurvival #SeeTheGame

item.title: La verdad no peca, pero incomoda.
item.dc:creator: xynova
item.description: Una figura impasible expone los hechos, mientras un oyente cercano se estremece ante el espejo.
item.sync:pageSocial:
"La verdad no peca, pero incomoda."
❓ Truth itself holds no malice; it simply reflects what is, acting as a neutral mirror, not a weapon. The discomfort comes from the listener's reaction to that reflection. You use it when you deliver bad news to a family member, knowing it will sting, or when you share a difficult but necessary professional evaluation and expect pushback.
AND: Honesty is a mirror, not a hammer. You hear it in a quiet post-mortem meeting where a failed launch is laid bare, stripped of corporate euphemisms. Or you tell a close friend their new business idea is a massive money pit before they sign a five-year lease. It stings, but it is necessary.
🔤 IN ENGLISH: • The truth hurts. • Hard truths. • Sometimes the truth is hard to hear.

item.title: Le busca cinco patas al gato para justificar lo injustificable.
item.dc:creator: xynova
item.description: Esa quinta pata solo aparece cuando las excusas absurdas intentan sostener lo insostenible.
item.sync:pageSocial:
"Le busca cinco patas al gato para justificar lo injustificable."
❓ You are inventing non-existent variables to force a broken logic fit, rather than admitting a simple mistake. It is like trying to give a cat a fifth leg to justify its wobbly walk. You use it when a politician offers convoluted arguments for a controversial policy, or when a child gives a far-fetched excuse for not doing their homework.
AND: If it requires five miracles to make sense, it is just wrong. You hear it when a colleague explains a missed deadline through a chain of cosmic coincidences. Or when a vendor spins a yarn about why the server crashed, making it sound like an act of God rather than a simple oversight.
🔤 IN ENGLISH: • Grasping at straws • Making flimsy excuses • Trying to explain away • Putting lipstick on a pig

item.title: Miente hasta cuando dice la verdad.
item.dc:creator: xynova
item.description: Un hablador astuto se topa con un oyente muy escéptico. Su historial siempre pesa más que sus palabras.
item.sync:pageSocial:
"Miente hasta cuando dice la verdad."
❓ Your reputation filter is on: past lies distort present facts, so you filter everything through a speaker's history, not objective merit. You use it when a politician states an obvious truth but still gets doubted, or when a colleague with a history of dishonesty makes a factual claim and you still don't believe them.
AND: Trust takes a lifetime to build and a single second to break. Someone always late finally has a genuine family emergency, but people still roll their eyes. Or a friend who always inflates their achievements tells a simple, true story about meeting a celebrity, and everyone just nods politely, then changes the subject.
🔤 IN ENGLISH: • You cannot trust them as far as you can throw them. • Take everything they say with a grain of salt. • They are a pathological liar.
